title_en: The staff and the creature of the earth
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff.
When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment.

chapters.summary_md: When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah says that when God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives a pair of moments: the decree of death with the creature eating the staff, and the falling after which it became clear to the jinn [c1][c2]. The statement about the unseen is made of the jinn: knowing the unseen would have kept them from the punishment [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says a small creature of the earth was eating a staff, and that was what showed his death [c1]. When he fell, the jinn saw that they did not know the unseen [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah teaches that knowledge of the unseen is not with the jinn [c2]. Another is that the ayah shows a death made known through an ordinary creature and an ordinary object [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who is meant; the ayah does not name him, and the inventory title identifies him from the verses before this one, which are outside the verses cited here.
- Not established: how long he remained as he was, what the staff was, or what the creature of the earth was.
- Not established: what work the jinn were doing, or how they came to know the matter; the ayah says only that it became clear to them when he fell.
- Not established: who is meant by them in the first clause; the ayah does not say who was not shown his death.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this event. None is used in this draft.
The ayah names no one; the link to the person named in the inventory title rests on the verses before it, which this draft does not cite. A scholar should confirm that link and its wording.
The word translated staff (minsa'ah) and the phrase creature of the earth are rendered plainly; a scholar should confirm.
